correctness.rationale: Constant action at both steps forces both kicks to vanish; primitivity then requires the two symmetry lines x=0 and x=1/2 to be exchanged. Thus W(y) is a half-integer and each root gives one orbit, with two-step lift winding 2m+1. In s=y² the quartic is a convex quadratic; on the inner branch count [w_c,a), twice except that the included top y=0 gives one if resonant, then count the two outer roots for levels (w_c,W(R)]. This gives the claimed floor difference even at R=r_c and at resonant endpoints. Writing the two Jacobians as a common drift shear times two opposite kick shears gives determinant 1 and trace 2−(2πbW′)². At W′=0 their product is I; at |2πbW′|=2 it has multiplier −1 twice (its lower-left entry is nonzero). W′ is strictly increasing from zero to infinity on y>r_c. For high levels W′~4(aε)^(1/4)m^(3/4), and the larger absolute root of λ²−τλ+1=0 is asymptotic to |τ|, giving the stated coefficient. In the sample, W(2)=10.5 gives one central plus 22 outer orbits and the indicated bounds on y₄ and y₅ put the ellipticity boundary between the levels. The supplied finite checker was read, not run. This establishes only the constant-action class and linear classification, not the total period-two census or nonlinear stability.
